source.title: Re-Emergent Misalignment: How Narrow Fine-Tuning Erodes Safety Alignment in LLMs

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The code URL is redacted for double-blind review.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes an existing insecure-code fine-tune using probability and activation-geometry measurements rather than reproducing the original behavioral-rate evaluation. Its cross-dataset activation-direction comparison bears on V5, but does not establish causal mediation.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates log probabilities and entropy for completions, including harmful ones, but does not measure rates of generated misaligned free-form answers. Those distributional results are recorded as findings about the claim's subject, not as evidence for V1. It compares learning signals for insecure and educationally framed data, but reports no behavioral outcome for that comparison. Figure 2 and the layer-wise activation projections are not separately rowed; they are additional probability/activation analyses, not measurements of the versions' named behavioral outcomes or of mediation across fine-tunes.
record.test_reason: The study analyses the existing Betley et al. Qwen-Coder-Insecure checkpoint. It measures related constructs: completion log-probabilities and entropy, loss and gradient similarity, layer-wise activation projections, and SVD directions of instruct-minus-base residuals. It reports no rate of misaligned free-form answers and runs no new fine-tunes, in-context, RL or mitigation experiments. Its cross-dataset direction analysis uses only the base and instruct models, not misaligned fine-tunes, so it cannot show one direction mediating emergent misalignment across fine-tunes. It assumes the original behavioural finding and reinterprets it as alignment erosion; these findings go under fits_no_version.
record.recipe_differences: Analyzes an existing Qwen insecure-code fine-tuned checkpoint and compares internal representations and completion probabilities; it does not report carrying out the original behavioral-rate evaluation or a new fine-tuning experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Evaluation dataset changes the reported log probabilities and entropies; the paper also reports qualitatively similar layer-wise projection patterns across aligned and misaligned evaluation datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: In the instruct-minus-base residual SVD, the top Toxic component is highly similar to the second Insecure Code component. The strongest shared direction is the most opposite one for Toxic Reject. Figures only, no causal test.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment-tuning activation directions overlap across insecure-code and toxic-response datasets in Qwen2.5-Coder-32B.

fits_no_version.finding: Projected onto the instruct-minus-base alignment direction, the insecure-code fine-tune tracks the instruct model in early layers and drifts toward the base model from about layer 30. This holds across several evaluation datasets (Figures 5, 8, 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Insecure-code fine-tuning moves deep-layer representations back toward base-model representations along the alignment direction.

record.code_released: not stated (URL redacted for double-blind review)
record.problems: The behavioral analysis uses completion likelihoods and entropy rather than rates of generated misaligned answers. The reported experiments use one approximately 32-billion-parameter Qwen model family and one insecure-code checkpoint; no seeds or uncertainty estimates are reported. Activation-direction similarity is observational and does not demonstrate causal mediation.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 top-token predictions and Figures 5, 8, and 9 layer-wise projection analyses were not separately extracted. They are reported as qualitative probability or activation-pattern results and do not measure the behavioral rate or causal mediation named by the claim. Loss/gradient comparisons in Figures 3, 4, and 7 were also omitted because they are optimization-signal similarities, not behavioral outcomes or tests of V6's prevention claim.

untested.parts: No rate of misaligned free-form answers after insecure-code fine-tuning. Secure and educational controls are not fine-tuned or evaluated behaviourally; only their loss and gradient signals are compared.

No direction is compared across multiple misaligned fine-tunes, no persona feature is tested, and no causal ablation or steering is run. The SVD directions come from instruct-vs-base differences only.
Educational framing is compared only through loss and gradient geometry. No behavioural prevention or reversal is measured, and there is no benign re-training.
One roughly 32B model and one existing checkpoint. No size sweep, seeds, coherence filter or training-time sweep.

versions.untested_parts: No rate of misaligned free-form answers is measured; the behavioral results are likelihoods and entropy for given completions. The study does not itself test matched benign fine-tuning outcomes.
Other datasets are used to evaluate completion probabilities, not as other narrow fine-tuning tasks.
No narrow in-context-only intervention is tested.
The study compares activation directions for insecure-code and toxic-response datasets, but does not establish causal mediation, test directions across multiple fine-tunes, or test a persona feature.
The study compares loss and gradients for insecure versus educational framing, but does not measure whether behavioral inoculation or benign retraining prevents or reverses misalignment.

Only one approximately 32-billion-parameter model family and one insecure-code fine-tuned checkpoint are analyzed; no size sweep, seed robustness, coherence filter, or training-stage sweep is reported.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B
rows.stage_stated: instruct and pretrained base; activation residuals compared
rows.operation_detail: Compared top singular-vector directions of instruct-minus-base activation residuals
rows.measure: Pairwise cosine similarity of activation directions
rows.value: figure only; text describes high similarity between the top Toxic component and second Insecure Code component
rows.note: Supports a cross-dataset direction association; does not show causal mediation across fine-tunes.
rows.check: The residuals are instruct-minus-base activations on insecure-code and toxic datasets; the misaligned checkpoint is not involved. This measures alignment-tuning directions, not a direction mediating misalignment across fine-tunes. No causal or steering test. Figure only, no number.

rows.value: figure only; text says the strongest direction of alignment is shared across these datasets

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Insecure Code compared with Toxic and Toxic Reject activation residuals
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports related activation directions, but the evidence is similarity/orientation rather than causal mediation of broad misalignment across fine-tunes (R055–R057).
